name: Gradual Blur
rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line description "Progressive blur reveal" only; no React Bits source or docs were read. A stacked, masked backdrop-filter band that sharpens content as it scrolls out of the panel edge is a common, reusable scroll affordance.

position.description: Which edge(s) of the host get the blur band.

height.description: Depth of the band, any CSS length.

strength.description: Blur at the very edge, in px.

layers.description: Stacked blur layers; more is smoother and costs more paint.

curve.description: How the blur rises across the band.

tint.description: Colour the band deepens towards at the edge.

fadeAtEnds.description: Fade a band out once the host is scrolled all the way to that end.

a11y: The blur band is an aria-hidden overlay; the host's content, reading order and accessibility tree are not changed or duplicated.
The band has pointer-events: none, so links and buttons under it stay clickable and text stays selectable.
With fadeAtEnds the band fades out at the end of the scroll, so the last item is always shown sharp and at full contrast at rest.
Forced-colors mode removes the band entirely so focus rings and system colours are never obscured; reduced motion keeps the blur but makes the fade instant.
